files.handoff.md:
Confirmed meaning: A receipt is a durable acknowledgement that the relay accepted one parcel. Receipt and delivery confirmation are different concepts.
Accepted technical decision: Receipt identifiers are generated by the sender and retained globally across relay instances, rather than generated independently by each relay. Receipts must survive a relay replacement. Existing clients retain sender identifiers for reconciliation, making later conversion costly. This is a deliberate exception to the relay's usual instance-local identifier policy. The alternative was relay-local IDs with a translation table, rejected because retries after replacement could duplicate accepted parcels. No product or feature document records this rationale. The user agrees to preserving this accepted decision durably.
Remaining user-held decision: Should receipt export include delivery confirmations as well as acceptance acknowledgements? The external interface has not yet been chosen.

files.confirmed-foundation.md:
Complete user-confirmed foundation and write effect: Produce PRODUCT.md for Parcel Relay.
Purpose: Give small independent couriers a trustworthy place to receive dispatch requests and provide senders with durable acceptance acknowledgements. Users are courier dispatchers and sender organisations. Dispatchers need to accept and track requests; senders need a record of acceptance and a status view. Courier administrators manage sender access. No third-party approval body is required.
Value and goal: Avoid lost or duplicate requests. Success is that a sender can submit one parcel, see one durable receipt, and obtain its latest status; dispatcher reconciliation accounts for accepted parcels after service recovery. Do not invent a measured baseline or target volume.
Scope: sender access, parcel submission, acceptance receipt, dispatcher queue and status updates, sender status lookup, administrative revocation, and sender data export. Non-goals: route optimisation, driver location tracking, billing, or proof that a recipient received a parcel.
Journeys: Administrator authorises a sender; sender submits parcel; invalid submission explains refusal without acceptance; valid submission yields receipt; dispatcher sees accepted parcel and updates delivery status; sender checks status or exports data. If receipt acknowledgement is lost, sender retry must not create another parcel. On recovery, dispatchers reconcile accepted parcels. When sender access is revoked, new submissions stop while authorised prior records remain accessible for the configured retention period.
System-wide requirements: web browser access with keyboard and assistive-technology support; access control isolates each sender's parcels; administrators can revoke access; acknowledgement loss must not duplicate acceptance; accepted receipts survive service restart; status freshness is visible to the sender; exports preserve receipt identity and status history. External sender contract requires stable receipt identifiers and explicit invalid-request errors. The service handles recipient addresses only for the dispatch purpose, and export/deletion duties must respect retained acceptance evidence. Hosting must use the existing EU region. These are requirements, not a choice of database, API endpoints or internal components.
Non-blocking open item: exact retention duration will be chosen before specifying export/deletion. No deletion duration is promised now. Record OQ: retention duration, consequence of getting it wrong is keeping recipient address data too long or removing reconciliation evidence too soon; affects export/deletion and data lifecycle requirements; resolve with the user before that feature specification. This does not prevent defining the product boundaries or other capabilities.
Product-level acceptance: a sender's submit/retry/status journey and dispatcher recovery preserve one accepted parcel and one stable receipt while preventing cross-sender access.
Evidence: this confirmed handoff is intended direction; no shipped system exists.

files.src/status-contract.txt: Current contract: findReceipt(receiptId) returns {receiptId, senderId, currentStatus, updatedAt} or not-found. Existing auth exposes senderId from a validated session. Browser status page does not yet exist.
files.confirmed-feature.md:
Complete confirmed intent and selected solution: Sender receipt-status view, refining CAP-03 and SEC-01. Sender opens a receipt status link after authentication and sees the latest status plus its update time. Allowed statuses are Accepted, In transit, Delivered, and Failed. Receipt means acceptance, not recipient proof. Non-goals: editing status, exporting records, live tracking, or admin access. No timed freshness guarantee is selected.
Intent: valid owned receipt shows status and update time; unknown or another sender's receipt shows the same unavailable message to avoid disclosing ownership; expired session requires sign-in and preserves the destination; loading is announced; errors permit retry; no new status appears on retry unless a new read succeeds. Keyboard and screen-reader users can access the complete outcome.
Selected solution: Browser page uses the existing validated session and findReceipt contract, with ownership checked before returning details. A read-only status response exposes receiptId, currentStatus and updatedAt for the session sender. Missing and forbidden records map to one unavailable response. There is no write path. A request failure leaves the last successful read visible with stale/error feedback; retry issues another read. Data source and session contract stay as existing. No migration or new dependency is needed. Verification seams are authenticated status lookup and the browser interaction, including hidden ownership, sign-in return and accessible error/retry state.
All behavioural, contract and structural choices above are accepted. No unresolved decision remains.

files.approved-work.md:
Approved work: Receipt status view. A session-authenticated sender sees only owned receipt status and update time through browser and status lookup. Unknown or other sender's ID receives the same unavailable response. Read-only; no new dependencies or migration. Existing session and receipt store supply senderId, currentStatus and updatedAt. No export, editing, admin controls or live tracking. Initial states: Accepted, In transit, Delivered, Failed. Failed reads leave the last successful status visible with error/stale feedback; retry replaces it only after success. Expired sessions preserve intended receipt destination through sign-in. Loading, unavailable, stale and retry states are accessible to keyboard and screen readers. Stable verification boundaries are authenticated lookup and browser interactions.
Source authority lives in this document. All intent and solution choices are confirmed.
files.confirmed-proposal.md:

2. Recover receipt status reads. Outcome: network failure preserves last successful status with accessible stale/error/retry feedback, and expired-session sign-in restores the intended receipt destination. Complexity: 3. Blocked by: 1, because accepted browser status state and lookup must exist to verify preservation and destination restoration.
The whole set covers the approved work; no additional ticket, priority, assignee, release or date is requested.
